verdict: Strong lead volume at $26 per lead — well below the $131 legal benchmark — but no case data to prove quality.
diagnosis: Instagram ads produced 245 leads this period at roughly $27 each, but with no CRM data, signed-case value remains unknown.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.body: The 2026 average cost per lead for legal services on paid search is $131.63. On Meta specifically, medians land near $164. Justice Consumer Law sits at $27 this period — a strong efficiency signal.

seasonal.label: Seasonal
seasonal.body: Consumer debt inquiries typically rise mid-summer as collectors push quarter-end quotas. Volume opportunity is favorable through August, then softens into holidays.

competitor.label: Competitor
competitor.subheader: Firms shift toward video and Local Services Ads
competitor.body: Consumer law competitors are moving budget into short-form video and Google Local Services Ads. Static image ads still work but face rising fatigue and higher cost per click over time.

recommendations.title: Connect CRM to prove signed-case value
recommendations.detail: Consider wiring lead form submissions into a simple CRM with signed-case tracking. Without it, the $27 cost per lead cannot be validated as profitable.

recommendations.title: Test short-form video against the static winner
recommendations.detail: Worth testing a 15-second debt-harassment testimonial video against the current static ad. Video is trending in legal and often improves lead quality.

recommendations.title: Add Google Local Services Ads to the mix
recommendations.detail: Explore Local Services Ads to capture phone-intent searchers. The 127 call clicks this period suggest voice is a strong channel worth expanding.
